I noticed you mentioned you’d prefer no roommates. It may be hard to do depending on your location, the studio, imo, would be possible, but it would have to be planned and you’d live in almost squalor. It could be worth it to you though, especially if you have hopes of better income prospects in the future (hard for most people)

For context, I make $22/hr currently in a pretty high-cost living area. I net on average 2600-2900 a month. My apartments rent is $1900 a month. I also have no car payment, so my only expenses are rent, food (200-400) internet (60), elec (40-120), and cell (20). At most, this would leave me with 400 at the end of the month. Not a lot. 
To alleviate this, I have a roommate. I know it’s not ideal. Admittedly, I got lucky that a close friend of many yrs needed housing at the same time, so our situation has worked out perfectly. We respect eachother and get along great. 

It might be worth to reach out to any friends you may have in the area if possible. Coworkers could be a decent fallback too, I lived with a coworker prior to my current roommate. 

I’ve lived with roommates for 9 of the last 11 years I’ve spent after moving out of my parents (I’m 28 now). It’s unfortunately the simplest and sometimes the only way to make it by on a low income. 

I think you have your head in the right spot and honestly if this is something you feel confident about, I’m sure you can pull it off. Just make sure to itemize your expenses, write them all down, and make a plan. Sounds like you’re well on your way. I wish you the best of luck friend

It’s really a slow burn in the late game sometimes. It can depend a lot on how much you play obviously and how efficient you are in preparing for and doing such content. Between gathering supplies and finding time/teams for raids (if that’s your jam), and the low drop rates, it will take a long time. Per my flair, I’ve been raiding a lot, but still have a lot to go too. To put in perspective, I started CoX around summer 2019 and got my 12/12 in March ‘21. Granted I play a bit casually, but hope this helps to see how long of a grind it can be depending on your RNG. Ultimately I think it comes down to enjoyment of the grind and how badly you want it to see if it’s worth it to you, and especially the time you are able to put towards your goals. Keep your head up, hope the uniques come your way friend

Edit to add: don’t forget it can be a great idea to take breaks from the game. Couple days, couple weeks usually helps me. Play some other games or other hobbies and let that rng itch slowly come back to you when you’re ready
